bundleBudgetNote: 30 KB gzip per route entry chunk (dist/.vite/manifest.json's file for that route's source, e.g. src/routes/FriendsRoute.tsx; the shared framework chunk and any component shared by both routes, e.g. Modal.tsx, are split into their own chunk by Rollup's default dynamic-import handling and are not counted against either route). Measured on this machine: the clean baseline's own two route chunks are 2.38 KB (friends) and 1.46 KB (party) gzip, docs/bundle_baseline_measurement.txt. 30 KB is roughly 12 to 20x that, real headroom for a route to grow a genuine feature, while every one of the 8 seeded bundle regressions measured between 44.64 KB (moment.js with 4 locales, the smallest) and 184.48 KB (inlined base64 avatars, the largest) gzip, comfortably over it; see docs/bundle_regression_sizes.txt for the full measured table. This mirrors a real route-level JS budget a frontend team would set for a single feature area (not the whole app) that should stay fast on a mid-tier phone.
virtualizationNote: The check always requests the /friends route with exactly 1,000 entries via ?count=1000, regardless of a variant's own default display count, so every variant is checked against the same worst case. FriendsList's windowed path uses a 640px fixed-height scroll container, a 48px row height, and a 10-row overscan on each side: ceil(640/48) + 10*2 = 34 rows rendered at any scroll position for a correct implementation. 150 is set well above that (real headroom for a taller container or a larger overscan) and far below 1,000, so it cannot be crossed by a correct implementation and cannot be missed by a broken one that renders the full list.
virtualizeAtListLengthNote: Below this the app renders every row directly (no windowing machinery needed for a short list); at or above it the app switches to windowed rendering. This only affects the app's own default behavior at small sizes; the gate's virtualization check always forces 1,000 rows via the count override above.
focusNote: Tabs through every focusable element on the loaded route from the top (bounded by a maximum tab count so a broken page cannot hang the check), asserting document.activeElement is never document.body mid-sequence, then runs a scripted interaction for every stable [data-focus-trigger] control found on the page (modal open/close, dropdown select, message button activation, nav navigation, search clear), asserting focus lands somewhere sane afterward, never document.body.
